image.alt: Frank Willett at a computer beside research participant Pat Bennett, with recording traces and a speech prompt on monitors.
image.caption: Frank Willett works with Pat Bennett in the Stanford speech-BCI study reported in August 2023. Implanted sensors record activity associated with attempted speech, which software converts to on-screen text.

video.title: New hope for ALS patients to communicate | 90 Seconds w/ Lisa Kim
video.description: Stanford Medicine introduces the 2023 research on decoding attempted speech from implanted recordings. The experimental system displays words on a computer screen.

items.title: An ultraflexible electrode beside active neurons

image.alt: Two-photon microscopy showing a yellow nanoelectrode surrounded by bright neuronal activity in mouse brain tissue.
image.caption: Two-photon imaging shows the electrode in yellow among active mouse neurons, two months after implantation. This is an animal research image.

image.alt: Gert-Jan walks using a wheeled walker beside researcher Andrea Galvez, who holds a laptop near a lake.
image.caption: Gert-Jan and doctoral researcher Andrea Galvez at Lake Sauvabelin in Lausanne. EPFL published this photograph with its May 2023 report on a brain–spine interface tested in one participant with spinal cord injury.

image.alt: Photograph of the miniature DOT brain stimulation device developed by Rice researchers and collaborators.
image.caption: The battery-free DOT stimulator receives power magnetically. The 2024 study reported temporary human motor-cortex stimulation and a separate pig study.

video.title: Rice team demonstrates miniature brain stimulator in humans
video.description: Rice’s report on the DOT research prototype and its magnetoelectric power transfer. The source describes temporary motor-cortex stimulation in a human participant; it does not establish treatment efficacy for depression. Video credited to Brandon Martin / Rice University.

items.title: Neural proteins revealed by expansion microscopy

image.alt: Expansion microscopy image showing colored synaptic proteins alongside neuronal processes in mouse cortex.
image.caption: Expansion microscopy reveals synaptic proteins and nearby neuronal processes in mouse primary somatosensory cortex. Tissue is physically expanded for imaging; this is a view of tissue structure, not a live activity recording.

items.title: Speech and expression through an avatar

image.alt: Study participant Ann faces a monitor displaying a digital avatar during a research session.
image.caption: Ann during training for the UCSF–UC Berkeley speech neuroprosthesis reported in August 2023. The research system links attempted-speech signals to decoded words, synthesized speech, and facial animation.

video.title: How a Brain Implant and AI Gave a Woman with Paralysis Her Voice Back
video.description: UCSF follows Ann and the research team developing a speech-and-avatar interface. The university article credits the video to Pete Bell.

items.title: Finding structure in neural population activity

image.alt: Gaussian-process manifold research graphic displayed in the Kemere lab’s machine-learning overview.
image.caption: The lab’s Gaussian-process manifold graphic accompanies research on extracting hidden structure from neural population activity. The overview does not identify a specific dataset or quantitative result for this image.
image.credit: Kemere Lab / Rice University (source attribution; individual creator not named)

image.alt: A thin, curved flexible fiber emits blue and green light, with a droplet resting on its surface.
image.caption: A flexible fiber containing sensing components and light sources, developed for studying communication between the brain and digestive tract. The June 2023 report describes optogenetic experiments in mice.
image.credit: Courtesy of the researchers / MIT News

items.title: Flexible threads for long-term neural recording

image.alt: Xie Laboratory illustration of flexible nanoelectronic threads for recording neurons.
image.caption: An illustration accompanying the Xie lab’s work on flexible nanoelectronic threads for collecting neuronal signals over time. It is a research concept visual, not a clinical result.

items.title: Cooling a nerve with a soft implant

image.alt: A thin, transparent nerve-cooling device is bent between tweezers and a gloved hand; its tip forms a cuff.
image.caption: A soft device with microfluidic channels and a cuff that wraps around a peripheral nerve. Northwestern’s June 2022 report describes an animal study of controlled cooling for reversible nerve conduction block.

video.title: Dissolving implant relieves pain without drugs
video.description: Northwestern explains the flexible, bioresorbable nerve-cooling device and its experimental mechanism. The accompanying article identifies the reported efficacy work as an animal study.

image.alt: A series of microscopy images showing cellular projections growing through microchannels over 14 days in vitro.
image.caption: Microscopy follows cellular projections extending through a microchannel device over 14 days in vitro. The Tringides lab uses such controlled environments to investigate interactions between neural and tumor cells.

video.title: Christina Tringides - Sontag Foundation "Distinguished Scientist"
video.description: An institutional introduction to Tringides’ soft-materials research and the CHAMELEON project supported by the Sontag Foundation. This complements the microchannel image but concerns a separate implant-development direction. Rice credits Jeff Fitlow and Jorge Vidal for the associated media.

items.title: A wireless cortical interface on one chip

image.alt: BIOEE figure showing a flexible BISC chip held between fingers, its circuit layout, a microelectrode image, and a device comparison chart.
image.caption: BIOEE’s BISC figure shows the flexible chip, integrated circuit layout, and electrode array. The linked lab source distinguishes 65,536 recording electrodes from up to 1,024 simultaneously recorded channels.

image.alt: A brace-restricted wrist undergoing assessment in the MAHI OpenWrist device.
image.caption: OpenWrist is shown assessing movement with a wrist brace in place. The lab’s rehabilitation program investigates robotic and wearable measurements of human motion.
image.credit: MAHI Lab / Rice University (source attribution; photographer not named)
